lead: A semiconductor laser is a forward-biased p-n junction that emits coherent light from a tiny crystal cavity. In a direct band gap material such as GaAs, injected electrons and holes recombine and release photons. The cleaved ends of the crystal act as mirrors, so light is amplified before it leaves. These lasers are small, efficient and easy to modulate. They are used in fibre links, barcode scanners, optical mice, CD players and laser pointers.
prereq: You need the p-n junction and energy bands (see Unit 7, Energy bands and intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors) and the idea of population inversion from 5.2.

sections.h3: Direct band gap and photon energy

blocks.text: A semiconductor emits light when an electron in the conduction band falls into a hole in the valence band. The energy lost appears as a photon. In a direct band gap material, the conduction-band minimum and valence-band maximum occur at the same crystal momentum, so the electron can fall without a phonon. GaAs is the standard example. Silicon has an indirect band gap: the electron must change momentum, usually with a phonon, so light emission is weak and silicon is a poor laser material.

blocks.where: λ is the vacuum wavelength; h is Planck's constant; c is the speed of light; E<sub>g</sub> is the band gap energy. With hc = 1240 eV nm and E<sub>g</sub> in eV, λ in nm is 1240 / E<sub>g</sub>.

blocks.text: The relation sets the wavelength. A larger E<sub>g</sub> gives a shorter wavelength. For GaAs, E<sub>g</sub> = 1.42 eV, so λ ≈ 1240/1.42 ≈ 873 nm, in the near infrared.
Only direct band gap materials give useful gain in a simple diode laser. Indirect materials heat up instead of emitting light.

The device is a p-n junction. Under forward bias, the n-side is negative and the p-side positive. Electrons are injected from n to p, and holes from p to n. In a thin active region near the junction, the injected carrier density becomes large. Recombination of electrons and holes then emits photons.

Population inversion means the occupation probability at the conduction-band edge is larger than at the valence-band edge. In terms of the quasi-Fermi levels, the separation must exceed the band gap energy: Efc − Efv > Eg, where Efc is the electron quasi-Fermi level, Efv is the hole quasi-Fermi level and Eg is the band gap energy. Forward bias alone does not guarantee it; the injection current must be high enough. The current at which gain equals cavity loss is the threshold current Ith. Below Ith the diode emits spontaneous light like an LED. Above Ith stimulated emission dominates and the output rises sharply. This is the inversion idea of 5.2 in a diode.
Two cleaved crystal faces at the ends act as mirrors. Light travels back and forth, is amplified, and a beam leaves through one facet.

items: Homojunction: one p-n junction of the same material; carrier confinement is weak.
Double heterostructure: a thin lower-band-gap active layer between two higher-band-gap layers; carriers and light are confined, so I<sub>th</sub> is lower.

sections.h3: Laser versus LED and where it is used

blocks.text: An LED is also a forward-biased p-n junction, but it has no optical cavity and no threshold. Its light is spontaneous, with a broad spectrum and a wide beam. The laser has feedback, a threshold, and a narrow coherent beam. Near-infrared diode lasers of the GaAs family (roughly 780–850 nm) serve short-range links and optical mice; CD players use about 780 nm and barcode scanners about 650–680 nm. Which laser for which task is covered in 5.6.

The threshold current is the current where gain equals loss. Below it the diode is an LED; above it the diode is a laser. The transition is sharp and is the main test in a laboratory. The beam leaves the tiny facet as an elliptical cone that diverges by about 10°–30°, much more than a gas laser beam; the cavity mainly selects a narrow set of longitudinal modes, so the spectrum is narrow.

examples.question: A GaAs semiconductor laser has band gap E<sub>g</sub> = 1.42 eV. Find the emission wavelength. Use hc = 1240 eV nm.
steps: The emitted photon energy is close to the band gap: E ≈ E<sub>g</sub> = 1.42 eV.
Substitute the values: λ = 1240 eV nm / 1.42 eV.
Round to three significant figures: λ ≈ 873 nm.
examples.answer: The emission wavelength is about 873 nm, in the near infrared.
examples.check:
Eg = 1.42
hc = 1240.0
wavelength_nm = hc / Eg
print(round(wavelength_nm))

traps: Silicon is not a good laser material: its indirect band gap needs phonons, so radiative recombination is weak.
An LED is not a laser. It has no cavity feedback and no threshold; its light is spontaneous.
Forward bias alone does not prove population inversion. Inversion and lasing start only above I<sub>th</sub>.
Use consistent units in λ = hc/E<sub>g</sub>. With hc = 1240 eV nm, E<sub>g</sub> must be in eV to get λ in nm.
Cleaved facets are the cavity mirrors. Do not treat the p-n junction itself as the mirror.

quiz.q: What is the active region of a semiconductor laser?
quiz.a: The thin layer near the p-n junction where injected electrons and holes recombine and provide gain.

quiz.q: Why does a direct band gap give efficient light emission?
quiz.a: The conduction-band minimum and valence-band maximum have the same momentum, so an electron can fall and emit a photon without a phonon.

quiz.q: A laser material has E<sub>g</sub> = 1.55 eV. Use hc = 1240 eV nm to find the wavelength.
Explain why an LED does not lase even though it emits light.
quiz.a: It has no cavity feedback and no threshold. Emission is spontaneous only, so photons are not amplified by stimulated emission.

quiz.q: What do the cleaved facets do?
quiz.a: They form the cavity mirrors. Light reflects back and forth, builds up above threshold, and exits from one facet.

quiz.q: Why does a double heterostructure lower the threshold current?
quiz.a: It confines carriers in a thin lower-band-gap active layer and confines light by refractive index, so gain is higher and loss is lower; I<sub>th</sub> falls.

quiz.q: A laser has I<sub>th</sub> = 20 mA and is biased at 15 mA. Is the output stimulated laser light?
quiz.a: No. Below threshold it is spontaneous LED-like light.

quiz.q: Write the wavelength relation for a semiconductor band gap.
quiz.a: λ ≈ hc/E<sub>g</sub>; with hc = 1240 eV nm, λ in nm is 1240/E<sub>g</sub> in eV.

beyond: Not for the exam. Commercial systems use quantum wells, distributed feedback gratings and vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers to control wavelength and threshold. Silicon photonics tries to combine silicon electronics with light sources made from direct band gap materials. Search next for VCSEL, DFB laser, quantum well laser and silicon photonics.
